note: THE ONE VECTOR SET of the registry's two bodies, the binding's and the endpoint's (REG-1.86; the canonical rule): every parser of the bodies -- skep-registry's, and any other a reader of the bodies builds (skep-resolve builds none: it calls skep-registry's parse) -- runs these in its own gate. The rule is the arbiter: parse(b) answers a record only where b == encode(parse(b)). `kind` is the kind the caller names, the link's type slot; `parse` is the parse's answer, `ok` (admitted: the bytes ARE the canonical form) or the refusal's cause as skep-registry's ParseRefusal::token spells it, which the daemon joins to its malformed_record token; on an admitted body `canonical_sigless` is the sig-less canonical projection a record-grade signature ranges over and `sig` the sig member as found (null where absent). A body carried as `bytes_hex` is bytes that are no UTF-8 string. The cap, 16 KiB with the sig member inside it, counted in the body's UTF-8 bytes and never its characters, is interim, confirmed at the registry's review round.

vectors.name: at_the_cap_with_sig

vectors.name: one_past_the_cap_with_sig

vectors.name: past_the_cap
